title: Cochain bounds and full embeddings for finite filtered localizations
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Use cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and decreasing filtrations [def-sp-filtration]. A uniformly finite decreasing filtered cochain complex $K$ has subcomplexes $F^pK$ with $F^aK=K$ and $F^{b+1}K=0$ for some integers $a\le b$, independent of cochain degree; put $\operatorname{gr}^pK=F^pK/F^{p+1}K$. Let $DF(\mathcal A)$ be the localization of these complexes at chain maps inducing quasi-isomorphisms on every grade. Let $D^bF(\mathcal A)$, $D^+F(\mathcal A)$ and $D^-F(\mathcal A)$ be the analogous localizations of complexes bounded, bounded below and bounded above in cochain degree, respectively. The natural functors from each of these three categories into $DF(\mathcal A)$ are fully faithful. Their essential images consist respectively of objects whose graded cohomology vanishes outside a common finite cochain interval, below a common cochain bound, and above a common cochain bound. Consequently $D^bF(\mathcal A)\to D^+F(\mathcal A)$ and $D^bF(\mathcal A)\to D^-F(\mathcal A)$ are fully faithful. All these assertions restrict to any fixed filtration interval $[a,b]$. The required bounded representatives can be obtained by good cochain truncations with induced subobject/quotient filtrations: if $H^n(\operatorname{gr}^pK)=0$ for all $p$ and $n<c$, the map $K\to\tau^{\ge c}K$ is a graded quasi-isomorphism; dually if all graded cohomology vanishes above $d$, then $\tau^{\le d}K\to K$ is one. These truncations change only the cutoff term and the cochain degrees beyond it and do not enlarge $[a,b]$.
